records.summary: 1701 Fillmore St is zoned NCT-FILLMORE (Fillmore Street Neighborhood Commercial Transit), where restaurant use is principally permitted. The site currently operates as a self-service/fast food restaurant (approved 2016-11-15 for continuation). The address sits within two Special Use Districts—Family and Senior Housing Opportunity SUD and within 1/4 mile of an Existing Fringe Financial Service—neither of which restricts restaurant uses. The immediate area is highly active: 14 food/drink businesses within 500 ft, including 4 bars, and 11 active on-sale ABC licenses within the same radius (53 within 1,000 ft). Within 1,000 ft over the last 10 years, only 7 dated use decisions are on file: 5 approved, 1 approved with conditions, and 1 denied; too few for a meaningful approval rate.

flags.flag: Zoned NCT-FILLMORE; restaurant use is principally permitted without a conditional use authorization.
Site has operated as a self-service/fast food restaurant since at least 2016; Planning approved continuation on 2016-11-15.
No change of use: the space is already a restaurant, and the concept remains a restaurant.
Super Duper Burgers is a formula retail chain (11 other locations), but formula retail controls apply only to new uses exceeding size thresholds; verify whether Sec. 303.1 applies.
High concentration: 14 food/drink businesses within 500 ft, including 4 bars, and 11 active on-sale ABC licenses within 500 ft.
Within the Family and Senior Housing Opportunity SUD (Planning Code §249.94), which does not restrict restaurant uses.
Within 1/4 mile of an Existing Fringe Financial Service SUD (Planning Code §249.35), which does not restrict restaurant uses.
Two formula retail CUAs on nearby blocks were approved: Pinot's Palette (2015, wine service) and Orangetheory Fitness (2019, fitness studio).
One restaurant CUA at 1865 Post St (entertainment addition) was denied in 2013; another CUA at same address (formula retail movie theater) was approved with conditions in 2023.

data_gaps: Formula retail threshold analysis: the records do not show whether a 2,950 sq ft restaurant in NCT-FILLMORE triggers Planning Code §303.1 formula retail controls when the use does not change.

The pathway rules state new use permission is 'not decided' because the existing use is restaurant and the description does not say whether that business stays; no definitive zoning answer is provided for a continuation versus a new tenant.
No extracted hearing transcripts or decision rationales for the two noteworthy CUAs (Pinot's Palette, Orangetheory) or the denied entertainment CUA.

ABC concentration metrics: the records flag undue concentration but do not show the census tract ratio or whether 1701 Fillmore falls in a high-crime or over-concentrated tract (not applicable here, as no alcohol is proposed).

No details on conditions attached to the 2023 AMC Theaters CUA approval beyond the four listed; unclear if any address neighborhood opposition or operational constraints relevant to other formula retail applicants.

comparables.why_comparable: Same address (1701 Fillmore St), same zoning (NCT-Fillmore), same use (self-service/fast food restaurant continuation). This is the most recent Planning approval for the subject property itself.
comparables.key_takeaway: Planning approved continuation of the existing self-service/fast food restaurant use at this address in 2016 via agency referral. The space is already established as a restaurant, so Super Duper Burgers would be a restaurant-to-restaurant tenant change without a change of use requiring Planning Commission review.

comparables.why_comparable: Directly across the street at 1700 Fillmore St, NCT-Fillmore zoning, restaurant use. ABC Type 47 referral approved in 2022 for non-formula retail restaurant.
comparables.key_takeaway: Agency referral explicitly notes the restaurant is 'non-formula retail use' and was approved. This suggests Planning tracks formula retail status even in routine referrals and may apply different scrutiny; the parenthetical suggests formula retail restaurants might require additional process.

comparables.why_comparable: Roam Artisan Burgers at 1923 Fillmore St (252m away), another burger restaurant in the Upper Fillmore NCD, ABC Type 41 approved in 2022. Very similar concept to Super Duper Burgers.

patterns.pattern: Restaurant-to-restaurant tenant changes in NCT-Fillmore are approved routinely through agency referrals when no change of use occurs. All restaurant continuations and health/ABC referrals for existing restaurants in NCT-Fillmore were approved from 2016-2023.

Restaurant use is principally permitted in NCT-Fillmore under Planning Code Section 760. Agency referrals consistently cite Section 760 as the basis for approving restaurant uses without discretionary review.

Planning explicitly flags formula retail status in routine referrals. The 2022 ABC referral for 1700 Fillmore parenthetically noted the restaurant was 'non-formula retail use,' suggesting Planning tracks this attribute even in non-discretionary reviews.
Not all multi-location restaurant chains appear to trigger formula retail review. Roam Artisan Burgers, a Bay Area burger chain, received ABC approval in 2022 without formula retail notation.

Agency referrals for restaurants in NCT-Fillmore and adjacent districts are decided quickly, typically 7-40 days from filing to approval. The median timeline for the eight comparables was approximately 15 days.

Adjacent neighborhood commercial districts (Upper Fillmore NCD, Japantown NCD) follow the same pattern: restaurant use is principally permitted, and continuations are approved through agency referrals citing the applicable Planning Code section.

risk.concept_summary: Super Duper Burgers, a fast-casual burger restaurant chain (11 other locations) with 65 seats, full kitchen, and no alcohol service, proposed for 1701 Fillmore St in the NCT-FILLMORE zoning district.

overall.next_step: Confirm in writing with the Planning Department whether Super Duper Burgers taking over the existing restaurant space at 1701 Fillmore St requires a formula retail Conditional Use Authorization or whether the restaurant-to-restaurant continuation is permitted through zoning referral, before filing…

approvals.summary: Formula retail triggers a Conditional Use Authorization under Planning Code Section 303; restaurant use itself is principally permitted in NCT-FILLMORE, but the rules did not decide whether a new use is established because the description does not say whether the existing restaurant business stays.

findings.text: The address is zoned NCT-FILLMORE, where restaurant use is principally permitted under Planning Code Section 760 and uses below 6,000 square feet do not require conditional use for size; the proposed 2,950 square feet is below that threshold.
Planning approved continuation of a self-service/fast food restaurant at 1701 Fillmore St on 2016-11-15 via health department referral, so the space is on record as an existing restaurant use.
Super Duper Burgers operates 11 other locations and is formula retail under Planning Code Section 178; NCT-FILLMORE requires a Conditional Use Authorization for formula retail uses under Section 760.

Two formula retail CUAs in the NCT-FILLMORE district within 1,000 feet were approved by the Planning Commission in recent years: Pinot's Palette (wine-service art studio) at 1981 Sutter St in 2015 and Orangetheory Fitness at 1633 Fillmore St in 2019, both after neighborhood notice and hearings.

Eight restaurant continuations and agency referrals on the Fillmore corridor from 2016 to 2023 were approved within 7 to 40 days, including a 2022 ABC referral across the street at 1700 Fillmore St that parenthetically noted the restaurant was non-formula retail, suggesting Planning tracks formula retail status even in routine reviews.

approvals.summary: Health permit to operate is allowed after plan check and pre-opening inspection; DPH will refer the application to Planning for zoning review, which is a step within the health permit process, not a separate approval.

findings.text: A food facility needs a health permit to operate under California Retail Food Code Sections 114380–114381 and San Francisco Health Code Article 8, issued after plan check and inspection without a discretionary hearing.

The health permit application is referred to the Planning Department for zoning review as a standard interagency routing step; this referral is not a separate approval and does not extend the health permit timeline when zoning is clear.

approvals.summary: Insufficient information: the rules cannot determine whether a building permit change of occupancy is required because the description does not say whether the existing restaurant business will be enlarged or intensified, and the existing occupancy group of the space is not in public records.

findings.text: Tenant improvements are described, which will require a building permit with plans, electrical, plumbing, and mechanical permits, and DBI will route the application to Planning for zoning review under Planning Code Section 175.

The proposed restaurant has 65 seats, which means an occupant load of at least 50 people, so the proposed occupancy is Assembly Group A-2 under the 2022 California Building Code; the existing occupancy group is not shown in public records.
Whether a change of occupancy under the Building Code occurs depends on the existing occupancy group and whether the business is enlarged, which only plans or an inspection show.

Neighborhood notification under Planning Code Section 311 is required because establishing a formula retail use in an NCT district triggered notification on the rules date of May 31, 2023, whether or not the use changed.

expected_conditions.condition: Must operate as a bona fide eating place if alcohol service is added later: meals prepared and served on the premises during all hours of alcohol service, with a kitchen open and staffed.
expected_conditions.basis: Seven recent ABC referrals for restaurants on the Fillmore corridor explicitly conditioned approval on operating as a bona fide eating place per Planning Code Section 202.2(a)(1), citing the location and operating conditions outlined in that section.

expected_conditions.condition: If a formula retail CUA is required, the authorization will likely include conditions on hours of operation, garbage and recycling storage within enclosed areas, and compliance with the San Francisco Recycling Program for compostable and recyclable materials.
expected_conditions.basis: The 2023 AMC Theaters formula retail CUA at 1881 Post St (94 meters away, Japantown NCD) was approved with conditions on hours (11 a.m. to 11 p.m.), enclosed garbage/compost/recycling storage meeting Recycling Program standards, and a three-year validity period requiring a building permit or site permit within that time.

expected_conditions.condition: Grease interceptor installation and FOG program registration required before the health permit final inspection, with equipment sized per SFPUC's Discharger Category assignment for the restaurant.
expected_conditions.basis: The San Francisco FOG Control Ordinance requires every food service establishment with cooking to install grease-capturing equipment; SFPUC assigns a category (1–3) that dictates device type, and an undersized or missing interceptor is a common reason DBI withholds final sign-off.

expected_conditions.condition: At least one certified food safety manager must be on staff and the certificate presented at the health department pre-opening inspection, and all food-handling employees must obtain California Food Handler Cards within 30 days of hire.
expected_conditions.basis: California Health and Safety Code Section 113947.1 requires each food facility preparing food to have at least one certified food protection manager within 60 days of opening; Section 113948 requires every employee who handles food to obtain a handler card within 30 days of hire. Health inspectors ask for the certificates at the pre-opening inspection.

expected_conditions.condition: Fire Department place of assembly permit and posted occupancy sign required before opening, because the proposed 65 seats means an occupant load of 50 or more.
expected_conditions.basis: San Francisco Fire Department requires a place of assembly permit and posted occupancy sign for occupant loads of 50 or more; the Entertainment Commission also requires the SFFD permit for venues of 50 or more. The pre-opening fire inspection must be completed before the health department final inspection.

filing_playbook.action: Request a pre-application meeting with the Planning Department to confirm whether a formula retail Conditional Use Authorization is required or whether the restaurant-to-restaurant tenant change is permitted through zoning referral.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: State that the prior tenant at 1701 Fillmore St was a self-service/fast food restaurant approved in 2016, the proposed use is Super Duper Burgers (a fast-casual burger chain with 11 other locations), no alcohol service is proposed, and the square footage remains approximately 2,950 square feet. Ask whether Planning Code Section 303.1 formula retail controls apply when the use does not change from restaurant to restaurant, and whether Section 178(c)(3) requires a new CUA for a change of operator of an existing restaurant. Request a written answer.

filing_playbook.action: If Planning confirms a CUA is not required, file for San Francisco Business Registration and then proceed directly to the building permit application with tenant improvement plans and health plan check; if Planning confirms a CUA is required, file the CUA application with the base fee and neighborh…
filing_playbook.what_to_say: If no CUA is required, the building permit application will trigger Planning's zoning referral review under Section 175, and the health permit application will trigger a second Planning referral, both of which are routine and do not require a hearing. If a CUA is required, the application must include a project description emphasizing that Super Duper Burgers is a locally founded Bay Area chain that sources local ingredients, that the existing restaurant use continues without intensification, and that the formula retail presence supports neighborhood-serving food options on the Fillmore corridor. Attach a good-neighbor operations plan, including hours, waste management, and employee training. Request the First Year Free fee waiver if eligible as a new storefront business.

filing_playbook.action: Submit the building permit application with architectural plans for tenant improvements, including kitchen layout, hood and fire suppression system, ADA path of travel, and finishes, stamped by a licensed California architect, and request routing to DPH, Planning, SFPUC (FOG), and SFFD.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: The plans must show three-compartment sinks, a separate hand-washing sink at each work station, all food-contact surfaces sealed and smooth, the commercial hood and Type I fire suppression system sized for the cooking equipment, the grease interceptor location and size (confirm with SFPUC before submittal), accessible restrooms, and the ADA path from the entrance to all public areas. If the existing occupancy group is B (under 50 people) and the proposed load is 50 or more (A-2), clearly note the change of occupancy on the cover sheet and include an occupant load calculation. Submit the DPH plan check application in parallel, with the menu, equipment list, and scaled kitchen drawings, so plan review runs concurrently.

filing_playbook.action: After DPH plan check approval, schedule a pre-final inspection with the DPH plan reviewer when construction is approximately 80 percent complete, then a final inspection before opening, and submit the health permit to operate application with proof of a certified food safety manager on staff.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Book inspections at least two weeks in advance. Walk the space against the DPH checklist one week before the final inspection to confirm hand sinks have hot water, all surfaces are sealed, food is stored six inches off the floor, and the hood suppression system has been certified by the installer. The health permit application requires the Business Account Number (BAN), the Location ID (LIN) from DPH, the federal EIN, and the food safety manager certificate. The FY2026–27 application fee is $470 and includes the initial inspection; the annual license fee for restaurants is $0 for 2026–28.

filing_playbook.action: File the SFFD place of assembly permit application at the Permit Center (49 South Van Ness, Suite 560) with the approved building plans and the occupant load calculation, and schedule the final fire inspection before the DPH final inspection.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: The place of assembly permit fee is $446 for an occupant load of 50 or more. The fire inspector will verify the hood suppression system has been installed and tagged, exit signs and emergency lighting are in place, the maximum occupancy sign is posted, and the path of egress is clear. An undersized or improperly tagged suppression system is a common reason the fire inspection fails, so confirm with the mechanical contractor that the SFFD has signed off on the system before requesting the final inspection.

filing_playbook.action: Register the FOG (fats, oils, and grease) program account with SFPUC Wastewater Enterprise and submit the Installation Verification Form after the grease interceptor is installed, to qualify for the 14.2 percent sewer bill reduction.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: SFPUC assigns a Discharger Category (1–3) based on the menu and cooking volume; new restaurants must install the grease-capturing equipment before opening. The Installation Verification Form must be signed by the licensed plumber who installed the device and submitted with photos of the installation. An undersized or missing interceptor is a common reason DBI withholds final sign-off, so confirm the size with SFPUC before the plumber orders the equipment.

filing_playbook.action: File the sign permit application with Planning and DBI for exterior signage, with drawings showing the sign dimensions, materials, illumination (if any), and mounting method, and a photo simulation showing the sign in place on the building facade.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: NCT-FILLMORE allows signage under Planning Code Section 607; the permit application is reviewed by Planning for size, illumination, and design compatibility, then issued by DBI. Processing typically takes 7–45 days. Window vinyl under the size threshold is usually exempt. If the building is in a historic district or is an Article 10 or 11 landmark, additional review time is required.

filing_playbook.action: Obtain ASCAP and BMI public performance licenses for background music, and register as an employer with the California EDD and obtain workers' compensation insurance before the first employee is hired.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Federal copyright law requires a blanket ASCAP and BMI license to play recorded music publicly; the two catalogs do not overlap, so both are needed. Annual fees are formula-based on occupancy and run approximately $300–$2,500 per license. Sign up online; licenses are effective immediately. California requires workers' compensation insurance from the first employee, even part-time, and EDD employer registration within 15 days of paying more than $100 in wages in a quarter. Set up payroll and insurance before opening to avoid penalties.

timeline_cost.notes: Timeline and cost are for obtaining the Conditional Use Authorization and health permit to operate, if the CUA is required. The CUA is the critical path: 120–300 days including pre-application meeting, formula retail neighborhood notice (Planning Code Section 311), environmental review, and Planning Commission hearing, followed by a 30-day appeal period. The base CUA fee is approximately $3,150 (CPI-adjusted annually); fees rise with construction cost, and a new storefront business may qualify for a First Year Free fee waiver. The health permit to operate ($470 application fee, $0 annual license fee for 2026–28) and building permit ($800–$15,000 depending on construction valuation) run concurrently with the CUA or after it is approved. The eight comparable restaurant agency referrals on this corridor were decided in 7–40 days when no CUA was required. These figures are times to approval when the CUA and health permit are granted; they are not times to a denial or withdrawal. If Planning confirms no CUA is required for this restaurant-to-restaurant tenant change, the timeline compresses to approximately 60–120 days (building permit and health permit only), and government costs drop to approximately $2,300–$17,000 (building, health, fire, sign, and FOG permits). All figures exclude state business registration, food safety certifications, insurance, and music licenses, which are listed separately in the catalog.
